questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following lanthanoid is diamagnetic?

Atomic no's $Sm = 62, Ce = 58, Eu = 63, Yb = 70$
questions.solution:
Electronic configuration of the given species are

a. ${Sm}^{2 +}\left(Z = 62\right) = \left[Xe\right]4f^{6}$ b. ${Eu}^{2 +}\left(Z = 63\right) = \left[Xe\right]4f^{7}$

c. ${Yb}^{2 +}\left(Z = 70\right) = \left[Xe\right]4f^{14}$ d. ${Ce}^{2 +}\left(Z = 58\right) = \left[Xe\right]4f^{1}5d^{1}$

On the basis of above electronic configuration, only ${Yb}^{2 +} \left(Z = 70\right) has no unpaired electrons i.e. has fully-filled orbitals. Thus, it is diamagnetic in nature.

$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Spin only magnetic moment of ${Mn}^{4 +}$ ion is nearly
questions.solution:
Electronic configuration of $Mn$ is $\left(Z = 25\right) = \left[Ar\right]3d^{5}4s^{2}$

$∴$ Electronic configuration of ${Mn}^{4 +}$ is $= \left[Ar\right]3d^{3}$

Thus, ${Mn}^{4 +}$ has $3$-unpaired electron and its spin only magnetic moment $\left(\mu\right)$ is, $\mu = \sqrt{n\left(n + 2\right)}BM$

where, $n =$ number of unpaired electrons.

$\mu = \sqrt{3 ( 3 + 2 )} . BM ⇒ \mu = \sqrt{15} = 3 . 87BM \approx 4BM$
